instruction: Review the spreadsheet on the desktop containing 2022 book reading records. Determine which book had the fastest reading pace in words per day, then open the empty 'book_list_result.docx' document on the desktop and record the book title there.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task asks to find the book with fastest reading pace (The Shining at 24767.16667 words/day, Row 11). Verified by analyzing all 10 books in the dataset. Evaluator checks if 'The Shining' appears in the docx file.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the final outcome: presence of 'The Shining' in the docx file
Getter logic is correct: extracts all text from the docx file using python-docx library
Metric logic is correct: checks if expected string appears in the extracted text with case-insensitive matching
Postconfig properly handles state: activates Writer window and saves file before verification
Expected value 'The Shining' is semantically correct according to metadata (fastest reading pace at 24767.16667 words/day)
Data flow is correct: VM controller gets file → docx parser extracts text → metric checks substring presence
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The metric uses substring matching ('expected in result'), which will pass even if the user writes additional text like 'I watched The Shining movie'. This is acceptable for this task but could be more strict if exact match was required.

Note: The evaluator verifies the final outcome (correct book name in document) but does not verify intermediate steps (spreadsheet analysis, calculation process). This is appropriate for outcome-based verification.
